## Tours featuring an Easter Island south-coast excursion and Anakena Beach

To see Rapa Nui's principal archaeological monuments without rushing back to the airport, allow several days on the island. The [private south-coast and Anakena Beach excursion](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/) takes a full day, visiting places where moai were carved, ancient ceremonial platforms and the ocean shore. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with this standalone excursion module on the itinerary.

One option is [“Easter Island: Three Days among Moai and Volcanoes”](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). The south-coast journey falls on day two, between visits to Orongo and the western monuments of the island. This gives you several dimensions of Rapa Nui culture instead of similar stops made just for photographs.

## What happens on the south-coast day?

The route begins at Ahu Vaihu and Ahu Akahanga. Their archaeological remains help visitors imagine island ceremonial sites before modern restoration work. It continues to [Rano Raraku volcano](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), where craftsmen carved moai from volcanic tuff. Statues at different stages of completion remain on the slopes, offering a direct insight into the work behind the stone figures.

The next major monument is [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), with 15 moai standing on a restored platform. Comparing it with Rano Raraku reveals the distinction between the quarry and the location where statues were erected. After a stop at Ahu Te Pito Kura, the journey continues to [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), near Ahu Nau Nau.

There is time for walking and swimming at Anakena. The final drive returns via Hanga Roa to the hotel. This is primarily an archaeological day with a chance to relax by the sea, not a full beach holiday packed into one excursion.

| Place | Reason to visit |
|---|---|
| Ahu Vaihu and Akahanga | Ancient ceremonial complexes |
| Rano Raraku | Moai quarry |
| Ahu Tongariki | 15 restored statues |
| Anakena | Beach and Ahu Nau Nau |

## How the excursion complements the three-day tour

The [three-day Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) separates excursions by theme. Day 1 visits Rano Kau volcano and the ceremonial village of Orongo. Day 2 is devoted to the southern coast, Rano Raraku, Tongariki and Anakena. Day 3 includes Ahu Akivi, the Puna Pau quarry and the Tahai complex, followed by an airport transfer.

A key feature is that a full day for the south coast is already included within three days and two nights. For travelers principally interested in moai and island history, this structure introduces archaeological areas in a logical sequence.

The tour's main conditions are also confirmed: 2 nights in a 4-star hotel, scheduled transfers, private excursions with an English-speaking guide, breakfast on days two and three, a packed lunch during the south-coast outing and admission to Rapa Nui National Park. Air tickets, medical insurance and additional services are excluded. A Russian-speaking guide is available at an additional cost.

## What to check when selecting a tour with this excursion

Rapa Nui is far from continental Chile, so flight arrangements matter as much as the island itinerary. Check the number of nights actually spent on the island and your arrival time: a full-day excursion is most sensibly placed between arrival and departure, as it is here.

[Rapa Nui National Park's](/chile/place/easter-island/) monuments are protected, and archaeological visits must follow access regulations. Check ticket validity, guide requirements, hours at individual sites and route restrictions before traveling. Even with park admission included, visitors must stay on designated paths and follow rules protecting the moai.

Shoes suitable for rocky trails, sun and wind protection, and water are useful for a day with many stops. Bring a change of clothes if you plan to swim at Anakena. Swimming depends on weather and sea conditions.

## Comparing similar programs

First consider **which archaeological areas are covered**, then whether they are spread over separate days. One full day at Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki offers a strong introduction to moai culture, but Orongo, Rano Kau and the western sites deserve their own section of the trip.

If the island is your main destination, start with the [three-day Rapa Nui itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). For combining the island with mainland destinations, explore [all Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [culture and history journeys through Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/). Another tour's mention of Rapa Nui does not, by itself, confirm that this particular private excursion is included: check its itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about south-coast Rapa Nui tours

### How long is the south-coast and Anakena excursion?

It is a **full-day excursion** covering several archaeological complexes, Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki and Anakena Beach.

### Are a packed lunch and guide included?

Yes. The private excursion includes a packed lunch and an English-speaking guide. The three-day tour also specifies national park admission.

### Can I see Orongo and Rano Kau on the same day?

The [three-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) visits these places on **day 1**, while day 2 is devoted to the south coast. The division leaves more time for the monuments.

### Are flights to the island included?

No. Air tickets are paid separately in this three-day program. Coordinate arrival and departure with the excursions.

## El Peral on a Valparaíso excursion

Funiculars reveal how Valparaíso works: the narrow lower city near the port is connected to neighborhoods on the hills. El Peral rises from Plaza de la Justicia, near [Plaza Sotomayor](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/), to Paseo Yugoslavo on Cerro Alegre. That makes the ascent and a walk at the top consecutive parts of a city visit.

Our [“Viña del Mar and Valparaíso: Quinta Vergara, El Peral and Paseo Yugoslavo” excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/) follows this route. El Peral is expressly named: it is a specific lift, rather than a ride on just any of the city's funiculars.

## How the ascent fits the rest of the program

In Valparaíso, we visit Plaza Sotomayor, ascend by El Peral and continue along Paseo Yugoslavo. Read separately about the [walk near the upper station](/chile/paseo-yugoslavo/) if a panorama of the port is your main interest.

This section of Valparaíso forms part of an excursion from [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). On the same day we visit Viña del Mar, including the [Quinta Vergara amphitheater](/chile/quinta-vergara-amphitheater/) and coastal avenues. We return to Santiago after the tour. It is a full-day group excursion.

## What to confirm before booking

If riding El Peral is essential to your trip, tell us when booking. Before departure, we will check whether the lift is operating and the walking areas are accessible on your chosen date. If this part of the route has to change, we will discuss the adjustment separately.

After stepping out of the cabin, the Valparaíso tour continues on foot. If you have limited mobility, discuss the whole route with us: boarding station, exit at the top and walk along the hill. We will check accessibility at each stop, including the sections beyond the funicular.

## The funicular on a longer tour

This excursion is included on day ten of our [15-day journey through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). After exploring the coast, you spend the night in Santiago and continue to Peru the next day.

For a separate booking, we can agree on the price, guide language and meeting point. If you are already staying on the coast, ask about joining before booking: the published route starts in Santiago.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which funicular is included?

The [Viña del Mar and Valparaíso program](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/) includes El Peral. We continue walking on Paseo Yugoslavo after the ride.

### Is the trip limited to the funicular?

No. It is part of a full-day excursion combining Viña del Mar and Valparaíso, with a return to Santiago.

### Can I ride the funicular without the walk?

The itinerary includes a walking section at the top. If you need a different amount of walking, we can discuss whether it is possible before confirming the excursion.

## El Tatio geysers at sunrise: steam, breakfast and a thermal pool

[El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) lie in the high-altitude Atacama Desert. In the morning, cold air makes jets of hot steam especially visible. Light begins to reach the mountains while white clouds rise from the earth, revealing a volcanic landscape.

We offer a **sunrise visit to the geyser field**, around **06:00 to 07:00**, followed by a **warming breakfast**, a stop at a natural thermal pool and a return to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) for rest. Exact departure times and overall duration are not specified; they depend on the arrangements for each trip.

## Why El Tatio is especially remarkable at sunrise

According to Chile's official tourism portal, the geothermal field lies at approximately **4,320 meters** above sea level. It contains many fumaroles and hot springs. In the early morning, the temperature difference between hot vents and the cold air makes the steam more visible.

El Tatio features **more than 70 fumaroles** and morning geyser activity. Visitors see an entire landscape of steam vents, hot pools and changing light rather than one enormous fountain.

The strength of individual jets and height of the steam vary. No particular intensity of eruption can be guaranteed. The excursion is best experienced as a chance to observe **a geothermal system** interacting with the cold mountain air.

## Safety near hot water

Care is essential in the geyser field: the ground can be unstable near hot mud, springs and steam vents. Stay on marked paths, never touch the water and do not approach steam vents for a photograph. Follow instructions from guides and site staff.

The cold is compounded by altitude. Fast walking and climbing can cause shortness of breath even for fit travelers, particularly when arriving from low elevations. Acclimatization, moderate exertion and attention to symptoms are essential. Significant symptoms of altitude illness require medical assessment.

## Breakfast after sunrise and the thermal pool

After the visit, enjoy a **warming breakfast**. Early mornings can be very cold at this altitude, so hot drinks and a break are welcome. The precise menu and additional services have not been specified.

Next comes a visit to a **natural thermal pool**, where visitors who wish may swim. Distinguish the scheduled stop from guaranteed swimming conditions: access may depend on site regulations, weather and personal restrictions. Separate admission charges, towel hire and pool availability require confirmation.

If you intend to swim, bring swimwear, a towel and warm dry clothes, but confirm the final packing list before departure. The transition from cold mountain air to hot water may not suit everyone; chronic conditions or difficulty tolerating altitude call for individual medical advice.

## What to bring to El Tatio

Above all, dress more warmly than the word “desert” might suggest. Below-freezing temperatures and strong winds are possible at sunrise. Thermal underwear or layers, an insulated jacket, gloves, closed shoes and a hat are appropriate. Sunglasses and sunscreen are useful after sunrise.

The trip requires a very early start, so arrange your meeting time in advance and avoid a busy preceding evening. An [Atacama astronomy excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-astronomy-telescope-evening/) is also interesting, but combining it with El Tatio with almost no sleep can be exhausting. Allow time to rest when planning a [Chile tour](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about El Tatio geysers

### When is the best time to reach the geysers?

The itinerary specifies a sunrise window of roughly **06:00–07:00**. Departure time depends on accommodation and transfer arrangements.

### Is breakfast really included?

Yes. A warming breakfast is expressly mentioned in Ada Tours' program; its detailed contents are not fixed.

### Can I swim in a hot pool?

The itinerary includes a natural thermal-pool visit, with swimming possible for those who wish. Actual access and individual restrictions must be checked for the excursion date.

## Tours with sunrise at El Tatio, breakfast and a thermal pool

[El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) are on Chile's Altiplano, at more than 4,300 meters above sea level. At dawn, cold air makes white columns of steam especially visible. The [“El Tatio: Sunrise Geysers and Thermal Pool” excursion](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-dawn-breakfast-thermal-pool/) combines a geothermal-field visit, warming breakfast and a stop at a natural thermal pool.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring precisely this excursion within a longer program. One linked itinerary is [“Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile: 16 Days from Uyuni to Patagonia”](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). The geyser visit takes place on the morning of day five, after travelers have explored the Bolivian highlands and arrived in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

## What makes this excursion day distinctive?

Sunrise is the main reason for departing so early. Visitors can observe steam jets, hot springs and fumaroles across the geothermal field. The program places the visit around 06:00–07:00. A high-altitude breakfast follows, then a stop at a thermal pool for anyone wishing to swim.

Prepare for severe morning cold at El Tatio. Chile's tourism portal states that the road from San Pedro de Atacama is approximately 80 km and takes around an hour and a half along a high-altitude dirt road. Actual departure time depends on road conditions and the particular tour. Dress in layers, with a warm jacket, hat and gloves, even when the desert is sunny during the day.

Altitude is especially important. The ascent from San Pedro to the geysers happens quickly, and less oxygen is available than at sea level. Travelers with heart or lung disease should discuss the trip with a doctor before booking. If you feel unwell at altitude, tell your guide instead of pushing through symptoms.

## Where El Tatio fits the 16-day itinerary

The [16-day Bolivia–Chile route](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) first passes through La Paz and the Uyuni Salt Flats. On day four, travelers cross Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and enter Chile, arriving in San Pedro de Atacama. An astronomy excursion is planned for the evening.

Day five combines two contrasting Atacama landscapes. **In the morning** are the El Tatio geysers, breakfast and hot springs, followed by a return to San Pedro and rest at the hotel. **In the afternoon**, travelers visit [Atacama's Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) for a sunset walk. The combination is memorable, but the day starts exceptionally early.

The following day takes travelers through Calama airport to Santiago. Later stages explore other Chilean regions: Torres del Paine, San Rafael Glacier, the Marble Caves and wine valleys. Choose this itinerary if you want El Tatio as part of a broader journey linking the Bolivian Altiplano with different parts of Chile.

## What matters about included services

We offer this 16-day itinerary in a private format with agreed hotels and transfers. The El Tatio excursion itself confirms sunrise geysers, a warming breakfast and a thermal pool. The complete journey's price is calculated individually: domestic flights, admission tickets and other services are specified in the full offer before booking. Do not automatically assume every condition of a standalone excursion is included without qualification in the overall package.

Compare two separate things: experiences included in **the El Tatio day itself** and logistics covered by **the multi-day tour**. Read the [full Bolivia and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) and compare other [Chile tours](/chile/tour/).

## How the El Tatio route via Machuca differs

We also offer a separate [“El Tatio and Machuca: Sunrise Geysers” excursion](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/). It is a half-day group trip with a stop in the highland village of Machuca and a visit to its local church. That module is included in the [9-day Chile journey](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/).

The thermal-pool version included in the 16-day tour explicitly features geysers, breakfast, swimming and a return to San Pedro, followed by Moon Valley. The Machuca version adds a cultural stop. Choose based on what each itinerary actually confirms, not on a shared photograph of steaming geysers.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring El Tatio and the thermal pool

### When do you leave for the El Tatio geysers?

The journey begins early so travelers can see sunrise near the geysers around 06:00–07:00. Confirm the exact meeting time and transfer duration for your particular itinerary.

### Can I swim in the thermal pool?

Yes. The excursion includes a natural pool with an opportunity to swim. Practical conditions depend on the site's status, weather and how you feel at altitude.

### Do I need to prepare for altitude?

Yes. [El Tatio](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) is above 4,300 meters. Consider previous high-altitude stages, hydration and your health. Time already spent in Bolivia does not guarantee adequate acclimatization.

### Is El Tatio included in the 16-day itinerary?

Yes, it is an excursion on day five of the [Bolivia–Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/). Detailed commercial terms, including flights and tickets, are confirmed in the specific offer.

## El Tatio geysers at sunrise: a walk and breakfast in the Andes

Sunrise at [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) is one of northern Chile's most memorable natural experiences. Before dawn, white columns of steam begin to emerge above the dark plain in the cold air, then sunlight illuminates the mountains and mineral surface of the geothermal field. Ada Tours includes **a warming outdoor breakfast** after the walk.

El Tatio lies high in the Andes at an elevation of over **4,300 meters**. Trips set out early from the [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) area. Sunrise is the ideal time because hot steam contrasts with cold air, making the plumes especially visible.

## What you will see in the geothermal field

At El Tatio, hot water and steam emerge through openings in volcanic rock. Visitors can observe fumaroles, small water jets and mineral deposits. Geothermal activity varies from one vent to another, so the scenery changes even within a single section.

The excursion introduces one of the world's extensive geothermal fields, with **more than 70 fumaroles**. Its focus is walking and observing the landscape. Low sunlight shining sideways through the steam is especially striking, turning white clouds into sharply defined shapes against the dry Andean slopes.

It is a natural area with dangerous sections. Water and soil temperatures near active vents can be extremely high. Remain on approved paths and follow guide instructions; a dramatic photograph beside a vent is not worth the risk of burns.

## Why breakfast here is particularly enjoyable

The high-altitude night ends with intense cold. As the sun rises over the plateau, hot drinks and breakfast offer warmth and a chance to enjoy the Andean scenery. **Outdoor breakfast** is the distinctive feature of this route.

The described program includes early departure, a geothermal-field visit and breakfast. A specific menu, serving arrangements, separate admission tickets and return time are not stated. Agree on the details when choosing the excursion, rather than assuming extra services are included in the price.

Another option is the [“El Tatio and Machuca” excursion](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/), which includes additional stops such as Machuca village and a thermal pool. If you prefer to concentrate on sunrise and breakfast among the geysers, choose the itinerary on this page. It does not itself promise a stop in Machuca or a visit to a pool.

## Preparing for altitude and an early departure

El Tatio is considerably higher than San Pedro de Atacama. An ascent above 4,300 meters may be difficult even for fit travelers. Allow time to acclimatize in the region before the trip; if you have heart or lung conditions or difficulty tolerating altitude, discuss the journey with a doctor in advance.

For sunrise, bring **a warm jacket, hat, gloves and closed-toe shoes**. Dress in layers: sunlight gets stronger after dawn, while wind and cold air remain. Sunglasses, drinking water and UV skin protection are also useful.

Chile's official tourism portal notes that El Tatio trips usually begin during the night, along a high-altitude dirt road from San Pedro. However, the exact meeting time, duration and vehicle type for this excursion depend on agreed arrangements. Do not schedule a tight flight connection immediately after the trip.

## Combining El Tatio with other Atacama experiences

The morning geothermal field complements daytime exploration of the desert. You could devote another day to high-altitude lagoons, followed by [stargazing with telescopes and a picnic](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-telescopes-stargazing-picnic/) in the evening. These excursions have different demands: El Tatio requires tolerance for extreme cold and altitude, while stargazing depends primarily on nighttime skies and cloud cover.

Explore other northern Chile options in the [San Pedro de Atacama excursions catalog](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and among [Chile tours](/chile/tour/). Plan around the overnight departure, your own altitude tolerance and sufficient rest.

## Frequently asked questions about El Tatio

### How high are the geysers?

The geothermal field lies at over 4,300 meters. Prepare for high-altitude conditions in advance, even though the excursion does not involve demanding trekking.

### Why go to El Tatio at sunrise?

In the cold morning air, hot steam forms especially striking white columns. The rising sun gradually lights the plateau and surrounding mountains.

### Is outdoor breakfast included?

Yes. Outdoor breakfast is explicitly included in the excursion description. The menu and other meal details are agreed for the specific trip.

### Does it include Machuca village?

This excursion does not list a visit to Machuca. A [different El Tatio excursion](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/) includes the village and additional stops.
